headline: Sales growth accelerates, margin holds steady
summary_short: Fastenal grew Q2 2026 net sales to $2,386.9M (+14.7% y/y) and net income to $382.8M (+15.9% y/y), with diluted EPS of $0.33, as operating margin held at 21.0% despite a 75bp gross-margin headwind from unfavorable price/cost.
summary_long: Daily sales rose 14.7% y/y on share gains with larger customers, pricing (+~290bp) and broad-based end-market demand; gross margin fell 75bp to 44.6% on unfavorable price/cost, but SG&A leverage (-80bp, employee-cost driven) held operating margin flat at 21.0%. Net income grew 15.9% to $382.8M as tax rate eased to 23.8%. Operating cash flow fell 4.6% y/y to $265.7M on AR growth from strong sales; the company returned $305.1M to shareholders (dividends + buybacks, 80% of net income) and ended the quarter with $204.7M cash and $120.0M total debt (2.9% of capital). FY2026 capex guidance reaffirmed at $310-330M; FASTBin/FASTVend signings goal cut to 27,000-29,000 MEUs from 28,000-30,000.

drivers.explanation: Daily sales grew 14.7% y/y, primarily driven by share gains with larger customers, pricing actions, and broad-based demand across core end markets; operating margin held at 21.0% as SG&A leverage fully offset gross-margin headwinds.
Growth reflects improved customer contract signings since Q1 2024, product pricing (~290bp impact vs 140-170bp a year ago), and a modest industrial-production improvement in H1 2026; FX added ~10bp.
Gross profit dollars grew with sales, but margin fell 75bp y/y to 44.6% on ~40bp of unfavorable price/cost plus smaller headwinds from customer mix, transportation costs, and rebates.
Operating margin held at 21.0% y/y as SG&A leverage (-80bp, led by employee-cost leverage) fully offset the gross-margin headwinds above.
Tracks the same operating-profit growth reported for Operating income above; EBIT is not a distinct line the release labels separately.
EBITDA growth follows the operating-profit increase above plus depreciation of $42.8M in Q2 2026 vs $42.4M a year ago; not a labeled release metric.
Net income grew with pretax income and a lower effective tax rate (23.8% vs 24.4%), reflecting return-to-provision adjustments and stock-option tax benefits this quarter.
EPS tracked net income growth on an effectively flat diluted share count (1,150.3M vs 1,150.1M a year ago).
Mirrors the diluted EPS move above; basic share count was also effectively flat (1,147.6M vs 1,147.5M a year ago).
Cost of sales rose in line with the price/cost and mix headwinds described under Gross profit; the release does not discuss cost of sales as a separate line.
Tracks operating-income growth plus a small swing in net interest (income of $0.2M vs $0.5M a year ago, on lower cash investments and debt balances).
OCF fell 4.6% y/y as accounts receivable grew on strong mid- and late-quarter sales (June sales +20.5% y/y), partly offset by higher accounts payable from increased purchasing.
Gross capex was $64.1M, directed at facility construction/upgrades, IT spend, and vending equipment; FY2026 capex guidance was reaffirmed at $310-330M.
Cash fell as $305.1M was returned to shareholders (dividends $275.4M + buybacks $29.7M) and working-capital swings absorbed operating cash flow.
Total debt fell to $120.0M (2.9% of total capital) from $230.0M a year ago (5.7% of capital); the release does not detail the specific repayment activity.
Current portion of debt rose q/q to $70.0M as more of the long-term debt matures within a year, while total debt (current + long-term) fell y/y; not separately explained in the release.
Equity grew on retained-earnings accumulation from net income, partly offset by $305.1M of shareholder returns and a wider accumulated other comprehensive loss; not walked forward in the release.
Diluted share count was effectively unchanged y/y and q/q; the $29.7M of buybacks was roughly offset by option exercises.
